initial_scene: Front-facing humanoid seated behind a worktable. A corded yellow-handled soldering tool lies horizontally on a black mat at image left, on the robot's right. Its dark base/holder is near the table center. Both hands initially hang above the rear table edge.

observed_sequence.description: Robot starts with both hands clear of the tool; yellow-handled tool rests on black mat.
Anatomical right arm reaches forward and down to the yellow handle; right fingers settle around the handle while the tool remains on the mat.
Right hand closes around the yellow handle and tilts the tool from horizontal toward a tip-down orientation; left hand shifts inward and forward nearer the holder without a visible grasp.
Right hand lifts the tool fully clear of the mat and carries it toward the center, with its cord following. The tool is held at an angle with the metal shaft pointing down and toward the holder.
Right hand moves the angled soldering tool toward the holder, guiding its metal shaft to the holder opening; left hand stays nearby on the opposite side without visible manipulation.
Right hand lowers/seats the tool into the base holder and loosens its grasp on the yellow handle.
Right fingers clear the handle and right hand withdraws upward then outward. The tool remains angled in the holder with its handle projecting up-left; left hand remains clear nearby.

arm_hand_roles.right: Active manipulator: reaches for the yellow handle, grasps and lifts the corded soldering iron from the mat, transports/angles the metal tip into the holder, releases and withdraws.
arm_hand_roles.left: Initially idle; moves inward and forward to hover beside the holder, then stays nearby. No tool grasp, transfer, or definite base-stabilizing contact is visible.
arm_hand_roles.coordination: Single-hand placement by the right hand. The left hand moves nearer the work area but no distinct mechanical support or hand-to-hand transfer is established.

anatomical_side_evidence.convention: Robot-relative anatomy, independent of image position.
anatomical_side_evidence.evidence: The camera looks onto the robot's front: the working arm at image left attaches to the robot's right shoulder beside the front-facing chest and head; the pale-palmed hand at image right attaches to the opposite, anatomical left shoulder. Native source initial PNG and frames 70, 200, 360, 510 and 597 show these attachments continuously.

inspection_coverage.sampled_frames: Every even source frame 0 through 596 inclusive, across all five sheets.

terminal_state: Yellow-handled soldering iron rests angled in the central base holder after the right hand releases and withdraws. The cord trails over the table; both hands are clear of the tool at the final frame.
uncertainties: The left hand hovers near the holder; the small native view does not establish any base-stabilizing contact, so support is not claimed. The interior of the holder is partly occluded, but stable placement after right-hand withdrawal is visible.
annotation_discrepancies: The original instruction calls the tool a soldering gun; the visible yellow handle and slender metal shaft support the more specific appearance-based term soldering iron. The stated placement into the base holder agrees with the observed released end state.
world_model_prompt: The robot grasps the yellow-handled soldering iron with its right hand and lifts it from the black mat. It carries the tool toward the central base, angles the metal tip into the holder, and releases the handle before withdrawing its right hand, leaving the iron resting in the holder. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.
original_task_instruction: Placing a soldering gun precisely into its base holder, requiring careful alignment and gentle placement to ensure proper docking.

selected_segment.reason: Complete original single-task reference; no cropping or trimming requested.
